pages.text: The $(thing)FM broadcast band$() runs from $(thing)88.1 to 107.9 MHz$(), one station every 0.2 MHz. Run your own station with the $(item)FM Broadcast Transmitter$(), and anyone with an $(item)FM Broadcast Receiver$() tuned to it hears you.$(br2)It is VHF: line of sight, carried a little further than 2m, and the antennas are VHF antennas. A 2m antenna works on it, though badly matched (about 2.8:1).

pages.title: Broadcast Transmitter
pages.text: A two-block cabinet. Pick your channel with << and >> (or the mouse wheel), then hold $(thing)ON AIR$() and talk, or speak into a desk microphone beside it. It goes out three times as strong as a radio, and its lamps light while it is on the air. It draws a lot of power on the air and needs a VHF antenna on its coax.

pages.title: Broadcast Receiver
pages.text: A walnut table radio. Look at it and scroll to tune, or open it for the POWER switch, the dial, VOLUME, BASS and TREBLE. It hears on its own wire antenna; an antenna coaxed to it takes over and hears much further. It draws very little: a power wire, or a $(item)Small Alkaline Battery$() (shift + right-click) for about two days.
